<STRUCT_0001>
A morphism of algebraic stacks which is representable by algebraic spaces
is quasi-DM, see
Lemma <REF_0001>.
Combined with the lemma above we see that the following definition
does not conflict with the already existing notion in the case
of morphisms representable by algebraic spaces.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of algebraic stacks.
We say <MATH_0002> is <TEXTITOPEN_0001>locally quasi-finite<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if <MATH_0003> is quasi-DM, locally of
finite type, and for every morphism <MATH_0004>
where <MATH_0005> is a field the space <MATH_0006> is discrete.

<STRUCT_0001>
The condition that <MATH_0001> be quasi-DM is natural. For example, let <MATH_0002> be
a field and consider the morphism
<MATH_0003>
which has singleton fibres and is locally of finite type. As we will see
later this morphism is smooth of relative dimension <MATH_0004>, and we'd
like our locally quasi-finite morphisms to have relative dimension <MATH_0005>.
Also, note that the section <MATH_0006>
does not have discrete fibres, hence is not locally quasi-finite, and we'd
like to have the following permanence property for locally quasi-finite
morphisms: If <MATH_0007> is a morphism of algebraic
stacks locally quasi-finite over the algebraic stack <MATH_0008>, then
<MATH_0009> is locally quasi-finite (in fact something a bit stronger holds, see
Lemma <REF_0001>).

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
Another justification for the definition above is
Lemma <REF_0002>
below which characterizes being locally quasi-finite in terms of the
existence of suitable ``presentations'' or ``coverings'' of
<MATH_0010> and <MATH_0011>.
